name: Human
behavior_desc: Humans have no yao instinct constraint; their actions are mainly shaped by personality, objectives, sect, alignment, and current circumstances.

name: Fox Yao
desc: Fox yao are naturally clever, skilled at reading expressions and moods, often striking in appearance, and commonly seen as having an innate affinity for opportunity and social ties.
behavior_desc: Fox yao actions should first show reading moods, social probing, advantageous trades, and a nose for opportunity. Ordinary personality may only shape the method; it must not turn fox yao into blunt cultivators who do not cultivate relationships.

name: Wolf Yao
desc: Wolf yao have strong bloodlines, value survival, hunting, and battle, possess keen instincts and swift movement, and often temper their cultivation through combat.
behavior_desc: Wolf yao actions should first show survival, hunting, combat, territory, and judgments of strength. Ordinary personality may only change how they attack; it must not make wolf yao sit in idle discourse for long or avoid all conflict.

name: Bird Yao
desc: Bird yao have broad perception and nimble movement, are born to yearn for distant places, and excel at scouting, escape, and exploring the unknown.
behavior_desc: Bird yao actions should first show migration, scouting, travel, observation, and evasion. Ordinary personality may only affect route and pace; it must not leave bird yao trapped in one place without cause or abandoning their need for wider sight.

name: Snake Yao
desc: Snake yao have subtle auras and patient ways, excel at hiding and ambush, are often feared by human cultivators, and adapt well to dark and dangerous places.
behavior_desc: Snake yao actions should first show lurking, patience, probing, indirect routes, and sudden ambush. Ordinary personality may only change how ruthless they are; it must not make snake yao into loud, frontal, openly bustling cultivators.

name: Turtle Yao
desc: Turtle yao are long-lived and steady of body, slow and cautious in conduct, and most skilled at defense, recuperation, and long secluded cultivation.
behavior_desc: Turtle yao actions should first show slowness, defense, recuperation, rest, and seclusion. Unless avoiding danger, breaking through, fulfilling sect duties, pursuing a clear target, or meeting resource needs, they should not move frequently or initiate conflict; ordinary personality must not override this guarding instinct.
